title: Sizing a wrapper to the flex-row parent's height actually sizes it to the tallest SIBLING — keep the shell's own rect height
trigger: A wrapper inserted into a flex-row (or wrap) container gets its height from parentHeight / max(sibling heights) on the theory that the row is 'sibling-stretch-driven', and the wrapper towers over the element it replaced — e.g. capped to the full viewport
principle: A flex row's height is the tallest item's height — not the moved element's slot. If the element WAS stretch-inflated by the row, its getBoundingClientRect().height already reports the stretched value, so reading the element's own rect preserves the original footprint exactly, for free. Reading the parent/sibling height instead only adds a failure mode: wrapped or stacked layouts where a tall unrelated sibling (a side info column) inflates the wrapper to browser height. Floor recalc measurements at the open-time rect so the reserved page slot is never under-filled, while still allowing growth when reflow legitimately makes content taller.

cases.context: kisskh episode page: player shell .col-12.col-xl-7 sits in Bootstrap .row (display:flex, flex-wrap:wrap) next to a ~1400px drama-info column. wrapperHeightStyle used min(parentPixelHeight, viewportCap) and recalc used max sibling height → wrapper became ~924px (viewport) for a 308px player — video floated mid-column with hundreds of px dead space.
cases.bad:
const h = isFlexRow ? parentRect.height : shellRect.height;
// recalc: measuredH = Math.max(...siblingHeights) || contentHeight
cases.good:
const h = shellRect.height; // original slot — always
// recalc: measuredH = Math.max(contentHeight, openTimeShellHeight)

applyFor: Computing a wrapper/replacement element's height inside a flex or grid parent with unrelated siblings
Deciding whether to read parent height vs element rect when preserving layout

check.command: Repro: Brave + kisskh episode page, narrow and desktop viewports — press 't'; wrapper must equal the player's pre-split height, .row must not grow.
